questions.question: What case ending does Jama' Mu'annath Salim take in the Mansub (accusative) position instead of the expected Fathah?
options: Tanwin Fath, matching the standard Nasb pattern
Kasrah, acting as a substitute (na'ib) for Fathah
Sukoon, because the word ends in a Taa Marbuta
Dammah, the same marker it uses in Rafa'
questions.explanation: JMS takes Kasrah in the Mansub position as a substitute (na'ib) for Fathah, making it one of the nouns where Kasrah marks two distinct cases: Jarr and Nasb.

questions.question: You see الْفَائِزَيْن and الْمُسْلِمِين. Which vowel before the Ya (ي) identifies الْفَائِزَيْن as Tasniyah (dual) rather than Jama' Mudhakkar Salim?
options: Fathah before the Ya (ـَيْن) identifies it as Tasniyah
Kasrah before the Ya (ـِيْن) identifies it as Tasniyah
The presence of ال before the word identifies it as Tasniyah
Dammah before the Ya identifies it as Tasniyah
questions.explanation: If the vowel immediately before ي is Fathah (ـَيْن), the word is Tasniyah (dual); if Kasrah (ـِيْن), it is Jama' Mudhakkar Salim. الْفَائِزَيْن has Fathah before Ya, so it is the dual.

questions.question: When declining قَاضٍ, in which case does it show visible (Zaahir) I'rab rather than Taqdeeri?
options: Mansub only — the Fathah appears visibly on the Ya
Marfu' only — the Dammah appears visibly on the Ya
Majrur only — the Kasrah appears visibly on the Ya
Both Marfu' and Majrur — only Nasb is Taqdeeri
questions.explanation: قَاضِيًا (Mansub) shows a visible Fathah on the Ya; in both Rafa' (قَاضٍ) and Jarr (قَاضٍ), the I'rab is Taqdeeri (hidden), and the noun appears identical in both positions.

questions.question: A word appears identical in all three case positions. Why might it still be Ma'rab (declinable) rather than Mabni (indeclinable)?
options: A word that never changes must always belong to a Mabni category
It may have Taqdeeri I'rab — I'rab that is present but hidden on the surface
A word is Mabni whenever its I'rab cannot be seen, regardless of category
Any noun ending in a Harf 'Illah is automatically Mabni
questions.explanation: Taqdeeri I'rab causes a word to appear unchanged across cases, yet the word is still Ma'rab. Mabni means the word belongs to a fixed grammatical category (pronouns, demonstratives, etc.) and receives no I'rab at all.

questions.question: When a Fa'il is مُقَدَّم (fronted before the Fi'il), how must the Fi'il agree with it?
options: The Fi'il takes the plural form for all Muzakkar Fa'ils
The Fi'il agrees in gender only and stays Wahid (singular) regardless of the Fa'il's number
The Fi'il becomes Mabni and shows no agreement markers
The Fi'il agrees in both gender and number, matching the Fa'il fully
questions.explanation: A Muqaddam Fa'il requires only gender agreement from the Fi'il; the Fi'il remains Wahid (singular) regardless of whether the Fa'il is singular, dual, or plural.

questions.question: If a word's I'rab is described as تَقْدِيرِي (Taqdeeri), what does this mean about its grammatical status?
options: The word's I'rab is optional and may be dropped in casual speech
The word has no I'rab whatsoever — it is Mabni
The word receives I'rab only in formal Quranic recitation, not ordinary speech
The I'rab is present but hidden and cannot appear visibly on the word's surface
questions.explanation: Taqdeeri does not mean no I'rab — it means the I'rab is real but hidden, unable to appear on the surface. The word is still Ma'rab and grammatically governed by its 'Amil.

questions.question: In the phrase وَلَدَا حَامِدٍ, what happened to the نُون التَّثْنِيَة (Noon of the Tasniyah) and why?
options: It was doubled to mark emphasis on the Tasniyah structure
It was replaced with a Tanwin to mark indefiniteness
It was preserved intact as an essential part of the dual marker
It was dropped (mahjoof) because the Tasniyah noun became Mudaaf
questions.explanation: The Noon of the Tasniyah is dropped (mahjoof) when the noun becomes Mudaaf. وَلَدَانِ becomes وَلَدَا before the Mudaaf Ilayh حَامِدٍ.

questions.question: In "إِنَّ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ" (Ayah 12), which device creates Hasr (restriction) — the claim that they, and none other, are the corruptors?
options: إِنَّ alone — it both emphasizes and restricts the predicate
The definite article (ال) on الْمُفْسِدُونَ, which restricts the predicate to the subject
The Dameer Fasl هُمْ alone — it separates subject from predicate
The combination of إِنَّ and Tanwin on the predicate noun
questions.explanation: The definite article (ال) on the predicate الْمُفْسِدُونَ creates Hasr — it confines corruption exclusively to them. إِنَّ provides emphasis and هُمْ creates the Mubtada-Khabar structure, but ال is what produces the restriction.

questions.question: What is the rhetorical function of the Hamzah in "أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا آمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ" (Ayah 13), and who were the السُّفَهَاء they referred to?
options: A grammatical conditional Hamzah; the sufaha' were the disbelievers of Makkah
A Hamzat al-Istihza' wal-Inkaar — mockery, not genuine inquiry; the sufaha' referred to were poor and formerly enslaved early Sahabah
A genuine question — the munafiqeen sincerely doubted whether iman was rational; the sufaha' were the Jewish converts
A Hamzah of affirmation to emphasize their own claim of belief to the Muslims
questions.explanation: The Hamzah is a Hamzat al-Istihza' wal-Inkaar — contemptuous mockery, not a sincere question. The sufaha' the munafiqeen referred to were early Sahabah such as Bilal ibn Rabah, Suhaib al-Roomi, and Ammar ibn Yasir (RA), to publicly degrade their social standing.

questions.question: To what specific behavior of the munafiqeen does the lightning-storm traveler parable (Ayat 19–20) apply?
options: Performing salah publicly when seen by Muslims but abandoning it in private
Reciting Quran aloud but internally rejecting its commands and prohibitions
Accepting Muslim charity while secretly sending funds to the enemies of Islam
Siding with the Muslims when Islam appeared strong and inclining toward the kuffar when they appeared stronger
questions.explanation: The traveler who walks when lightning flashes and freezes in darkness mirrors the munafiqeen's political wavering: they aligned with the believers when Islam was ascendant and shifted toward the kuffar when they appeared more powerful.

questions.question: What does إِلْتِفَات (iltifat) achieve when Allah shifts from third-person description of the three groups to direct address in "يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ" (Ayah 21)?
options: It creates a Hasr (restriction) that limits the command to the specific audience being addressed
It activates and startles the listener, signaling that what follows is of the utmost critical importance
It indicates a shift in time frame from past events to a present obligation
It signals that the verse abrogates the description of the three groups that preceded it
questions.explanation: Iltifat is a rhetorical turn toward the audience with direct address. Its effect is to startle and fully engage the listener — Allah uses it because most people are heedless (ghafiloon) of the most critical truths, and direct address forces engagement that third-person description cannot.

questions.question: In the second parable (Ayat 19–20), what does صَيِّب describe — is it a gentle rain or something more intense?
options: A very heavy, torrential downpour — not a gentle or moderate rain
A gentle spring shower that gradually nourishes the earth and crops
A persistent drizzle that accumulates slowly over many days
A seasonal mist associated with cool highland weather in Arabia
questions.explanation: صَيِّب refers to a very heavy, torrential rain shower. Its intensity is part of the parable's force — the munafiqeen are engulfed in a violent storm, not a mild inconvenience.

questions.question: In the context of divine dealings, what does إِمْلَاء (giving someone imla') mean — and what does it NOT signify?
options: It means giving respite and delaying punishment; it is not a sign of divine approval or safety
It means recording deeds for judgment; it indicates a neutral and suspended divine stance
It means permanent forgiveness; it signals that the sin has been overlooked entirely
It means immediate punishment; it always signals Allah's active anger at the transgressor
questions.explanation: Imla' means to give respite — to delay punishment while allowing the transgressor to continue. Being given imla' is itself a form of punishment, extending their rope before a final, severe reckoning. It is never a sign of divine approval.

questions.question: What does إِلْتِفَات signal each time Allah uses "يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ" or "يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا"?
options: A command or reminder of the highest importance, directed at an audience prone to heedlessness
A signal that the verse following it abrogates the one immediately before it
A change of grammatical subject indicating that a new group is being described
An indication that the verse was revealed in response to a specific question from the Sahabah
questions.explanation: Iltifat signals a rhetorical "turning toward" — a direct address used whenever Allah wants to convey something of the utmost importance to people who tend to be heedless. The sudden shift commands full attention.

questions.question: Why is human skin permanently excluded from the purifying effect of Dabaghat (tanning)?
options: Out of respect for human dignity (karāmat al-insān) — not because the skin is inherently impure
Because no known tanning substance can physically purify human skin according to Hanafi criteria
Because Imam Abu Hanifa ruled by analogy that whatever is forbidden to eat is also forbidden to tan
Because human skin is considered najis in essence (najasah 'ayniyyah) like pig skin
questions.explanation: Human skin is excluded not because it is najis but out of karamat al-adam — respect for human dignity. Using it would be a violation of that dignity. Pig skin, by contrast, is excluded because it is najis in its very essence.

questions.question: What is the Hanafi principle underlying the ruling that hair, bone, hoof, and similar parts of a dead animal (mayta) remain pure without tanning?
options: Any part of the animal that contains no life — no blood, no sensation — remains pure even after death
Any part that was halal to eat while the animal was alive remains ritually pure after its death
Any part covered by the hide is purified when the hide is tanned after the animal's death
Any part that does not touch the ground at the moment of slaughter is unaffected by death impurity
questions.explanation: The Hanafi principle is that parts with no life — no coursing blood, no sensation — are unaffected by death and therefore remain pure. Imam al-Shafi'i disagrees: in his position all eight such parts are najis and unusable from a mayta.

questions.question: What is the mu'tamad (operative fatwa) position for purifying a مَعِين (constantly replenishing) well, and who is credited with it?
options: Remove 100 buckets — a middle position attributed to Imam Abu Yusuf
Remove 40 buckets of average local size — the position of Imam Abu Hanifa
Drain the well entirely and allow it to refill — the position agreed upon by all three Hanafi Imams
Remove 200 to 300 buckets of average local size — the position of Imam Muhammad al-Shaybani
questions.explanation: The mu'tamad Hanafi position is that of Imam Muhammad al-Shaybani: remove 200 to 300 buckets of average local size. This is practical without requiring physical entry into the well or waiting for a complete refill.

questions.question: A person prayed all day using water from a well, then discovered a small, non-swollen dead mouse had been in it the whole time. According to Imam Abu Hanifa, what must they repeat?
options: Only wudu must be redone; the prayers themselves are valid and do not need repeating
All prayers performed that day, from the start of the day until the moment of discovery
Only the last prayer performed before the discovery — earlier ones are covered by the principle of hardship
Nothing — the mouse being small and non-swollen means the water was never impure
questions.explanation: According to Imam Abu Hanifa, discovering a small, non-swollen dead animal in a well retroactively impugns the water for the entire day. All prayers performed that day must be repeated.

questions.question: Can الدِّبَاغَة الحُكُمِيَّة (constructive tanning) purify a hide without any tanning substance being physically applied to it?
options: Only when the dried hide is subsequently washed in running water at least three times
Yes — natural drying by open air, sun, and soil is sufficient under the Hanafi position
No — a chemical or physical tanning agent must always make contact with the hide for purification
Only if the animal was halal to slaughter while alive — otherwise hakiki tanning is required
questions.explanation: Hukmi (constructive) dabagha means the hide is purified by natural drying — exposure to open air, sun, and soil — with no substance applied. Under the Hanafi position this is sufficient for purification.

questions.question: When only donkey su'r is available and its ruling is مَشْكُوك (doubtful), what is the practical ruling for a person who needs to purify for salah?
options: Use the su'r for wudu and pray — evidential doubt does not invalidate a purification already performed
Perform both wudu with the su'r and tayammum, then proceed with salah
Perform tayammum only — a mashkuk liquid may not be used for purification at all
Delay salah until certain water is found — the prayer would otherwise be invalid
questions.explanation: Since the ruling on donkey su'r is uncertain, the Ahnaf require combining both wudu and tayammum — covering all possibilities — so the salah is valid regardless of which ruling is correct.

questions.question: In well contamination rulings, what does التَّفَسُّخ refer to — and how does its presence change the ruling?
options: The stage of decomposition where the body swells and cracks open, triggering full drainage regardless of animal size
The smell of the water changing, which always requires draining an extra fifty buckets beyond the standard amount
The initial moment of the animal's death, which immediately requires removing the maximum bucket amount
The color change of the water — when visible, the standard bucket amounts are doubled
questions.explanation: Tafassukh refers to the body swelling and beginning to crack open — advanced decomposition. When this stage is reached, the entire well must be emptied no matter how small the animal was, because the contamination has spread throughout the water.
